A1.justification: Both PDFs describe Cambrian-P and contain readable main text and Appendices A–C. All 16 tables and 12 figures can be matched across versions; pagination changes do not create material gaps.

before.justification: v1 reports original Cambrian-P benchmark results, pose-estimation experiments, ablations, and qualitative analyses, including Tables 1–16 and the appendix figures.

after.justification: v2 retains these original experiments, including the 73.7 VSI-Bench score in Table 1, camera-pose results in Table 5, and appendix evaluations and analyses.

M1.justification: The architecture, losses, interleaved training, and pseudo-pose pipeline are retained. The two learnable queries were already defined in v1 Section 3.1; v2 clarifies introductory descriptions, token usage, and the existing jitter procedure without establishing an algorithm change.

E1.justification: Training sources and evaluated tasks remain the same, including spatial/general VQA, ScanNet, TUM-dynamic, Sintel, and appendix ReVSI evaluation. Changes such as VSTemporalI-Bench to VSTI-Bench standardize names rather than add coverage.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged in the corresponding benchmark and latency tables. Table 7 explicitly labels the existing 67.3 baseline as Cambrian-P without pose; corrected MASt3R and LLaVA-NeXT citations do not introduce different evaluated methods.

E3.justification: No changed splits, budgets, metrics, or experimental controls are established. Section 5.1 explains the relationship between training length and existing 90-frame evaluation. Appendix A.2 distinguishes uniform VQA sampling from dynamic pose-only sampling, consistent with v1 Sections 3.3 and A.1.

E4.justification: The component, frame-count, loss, inference-token, and scaling analyses are retained. Appendix depth-baseline sweeps, pose-data scaling, ReVSI analysis, trajectory comparisons, and qualitative examples test the same questions with the same evidence.

E5.justification: Both versions retain the same point-estimate and averaging practices. Neither adds or revises repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, error bars, or statistical significance tests.

E6.justification: Table data values and plotted results are unchanged, but numerical summaries are corrected. Section 7.1 changes approximately 3% to 3.9 points, matching Table 8's 71.2 minus 67.3. Table 2's camera-movement gain is clarified as 20.0 percentage points, matching 87.7 minus 67.7. These are reporting corrections, not new performance gains.

T1.justification: Pose encoding, loss definitions, normalization, and scale-alignment mathematics are retained. The new displayed jitter equations in Section 3.3 and Appendix A.1 make the previously described clipping and monotonic ordering explicit; they clarify the specification without substantive new theoretical reasoning or proofs.

C1.justification: The abstract narrows the broad state-of-the-art streaming pose-estimation claim to best ScanNet ATE among streaming methods, matching Table 5's metric-specific evidence. The central contribution and claims about pose supervision improving video understanding remain.

C2.justification: The explanations involving global spatial reasoning, learned representations, pose versus depth supervision, and VQA pretraining are retained. Appendix B.1 already discussed ReVSI frame-budget mismatch and annotation distribution shift; these limitations are not newly introduced.

D1.justification: v2 specifies integer jitter offsets and recursive monotonicity enforcement, clarifies sampling and loss assignments in Appendix A.2, and explains training versus inference sequence lengths. Appendix A.3 also corrects the pipeline-stage summary and explicitly lists both field-of-view components. These refine documentation of retained procedures.

R1.justification: The bibliography replaces the MASt3R-SLAM reference with the original MASt3R paper and adds LLaVA-NeXT for the existing Table 2 comparator. InternVL-3.5 attribution is also corrected. The broader related-work discussion and research positioning remain unchanged.

P1.justification: Localized edits standardize benchmark/model names, clarify sampling and token descriptions, and correct gain terminology. Shang-Wen Li is added to the author list. The section organization and overall narrative are retained.

P2.justification: Figures 1–2 receive clearer captions, Table 7 visually separates and labels the no-pose baseline, and Table 1 moves from page 8 to page 9 with accompanying reflow. The figure artwork is retained, with no added or removed figures or tables.

improvement.justification: v2 improves reporting accuracy by qualifying the abstract's pose-estimation claim, correcting numerical gain descriptions, and fixing baseline references and labels. Clearer sampling and token-use documentation also reduces reproducibility ambiguities. These are useful, limited corrections; the experimental evidence and substantive conclusions remain stable.
